key_highlights: ASX shed $90bn in a week as rate-rise fears and oil price surge pressured miners and banks
Iron ore entering a 'bloodletting' phase, pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX
AUD weakened sharply on Australian growth scare, complicating import costs and commodity demand
RBA flagged rental inflation as a key concern, limiting near-term rate-cut expectations
Oil prices volatile: IEA demand forecast vs. supply suppression failure creating two-way risk
ANZ.AX restructuring post-3,500 job cuts signals ongoing cost pressure across financials
Housing correction deepens with no spring bounce in auctions; first-home buyer surge noted
Santos (STO.AX) preservation via policy concessions; gas supply rules softened for Asia
Superannuation reform debate intensifies with populist pressure vs. institutional concerns
Small-cap mining active: PolarX, Sunstone Metals, Manuka Resources; Canaccord-led cap raises

sectors.trend: Sharp negative. Iron ore 'bloodletting' underway; ASX miners leading the $90bn selloff. Small-caps (PolarX, Sunstone, Manuka) showing relative strength via cap raises.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin compression. Gold (Kuniko, #75) and battery tech (Critical Resources, #74) offer diversification. Canaccord-led cap raises (#51) signal capital-hungry exploration phase.

sectors.trend: Negative. Rising bond yields and rate fears pressure valuations. ANZ.AX restructuring post-3,500 cuts signals industry-wide cost discipline. JPMorgan private bank expansion (#30) signals global capital reallocation.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX, ANZ.AX face NIM pressure if RBA holds rates. Net interest margins may stabilise but credit growth slows with business pessimism (#59).

sectors.trend: Mixed-to-volatile. Oil 'explodes' on supply suppression failure (#61) but IEA forecasts demand drop (#35). Australian fuel prices to rise 30c (#48). Santos preserved via policy (#54); gas rules softened (#73).
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, BRL.AX, STO.AX benefit from oil upside but face demand-risk. LNG exporters gain from Asia gas demand. Fuel cost pass-through pressures consumer staples.

sectors.trend: Under pressure. Woolworths (WES.AX) caught raising prices during 'Price Freeze' (#62). Falling house prices boost first-home buyers (#63) but business confidence weak (#59).
sectors.implications: WES.AX, CPL.AX face margin squeeze from input costs. Housing correction may support discretionary spend but income effect negative.

sectors.trend: Neutral-to-positive. Kestra cardiovascular earnings in spotlight (#39). AI development slowdown calls (#11) create uncertainty for tech. CSL.AX relatively insulated.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX defensive. AI infrastructure names (Forgent, #39) volatile. Domestic tech limited exposure.

sectors.trend: Negative. No spring bounce in auctions (#26). Housing prices crashing (#63). RBA rental inflation concern (#70) limits rate-cut catalyst for property valuations.
sectors.implications: GPW.AX, DGL.AX, ICPS.AX face occupancy and yield pressure. Falling prices may attract value buyers long-term.

key_themes: Rate-rise fears and rising bond yields driving broad ASX selloff
Iron ore structural demand concern (China) triggering commodity bloodletting
AUD weakness amplifying import inflation and complicating RBA policy
RBA trapped between rental inflation and growth slowdown
Oil supply-demand tug-of-war creating energy volatility
Housing correction: pain for sellers, opportunity for first-home buyers
Superannuation reform debate: populism vs. fiscal sustainability
Small-cap mining capital raises signal exploration optimism despite macro headwinds
Business confidence deteriorating; tax burden perception rising
Geopolitical risk: Yemen conflict, Arctic shipping, China trade routes

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Iron ore price collapse / China demand slowdown
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce exposure to pure-play iron ore (FMG.AX, RIO.AX); diversify into gold and battery metals

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA policy trap: rental inflation vs. growth scare
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hold duration-neutral; favour equities with pricing power over rate-sensitive REITs
Hedge AUD exposure; favour domestic-revenue companies (WES.AX, CSL.AX)
Avoid directional oil bets; favour integrated majors (WDS.AX) over pure explorers
Monitor auction clearance rates; consider REIT value entry on further weakness
Maintain liquidity; monitor LNG shipping costs for energy sector

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold and battery metals as iron ore weakens
opportunities.rationale: Iron ore bloodletting shifts capital to alternative commodities; Kuniko and Critical Resources showing relative strength

opportunities.recommendation: Selective entry into quality REITs on housing correction
opportunities.rationale: No spring bounce signals further downside but creates value entry for income-focused investors

opportunities.recommendation: Hold defensive healthcare and consumer staples
opportunities.rationale: CSL.AX and WES.AX offer resilience amid growth scare; WES pricing power despite Price Freeze optics

opportunities.recommendation: Monitor small-cap mining cap raises for momentum
opportunities.rationale: Canaccord-led raises and PolarX/Sunstone/Manuka strength signal exploration sector rotation

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce pure-play iron ore and coal exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Bloodletting phase with no clear floor; China demand risk unresolved

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge AUD weakness via short AUD or long USD positions
defensive_moves.rationale: Growth scare and RBA policy trap limit AUD recovery; import inflation risk

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain cash buffer; avoid leverage in rate-uncertain environment
defensive_moves.rationale: RBA trapped; bond yields rising; $90bn ASX loss signals further downside risk

market_outlook.short_term: Bearish. ASX likely to test lower supports as iron ore weakness, rising yields, and AUD pressure persist. RBA on hold due to rental inflation. Expect continued miner/bank underperformance. 1-3 month: ^AXJO down 3-5% further.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautiously constructive. Housing correction may stabilise within 6-12 months. Superannuation reform could unlock capital flows. Iron ore likely to find floor. Energy transition (battery metals, LNG) provides structural support. Key variable: RBA timing and China stimulus.

Iron ore contract price trajectory (62% Fe) and China property data
AUD/USD reaction to US CPI and Fed Chair commentary
ANZ.AX and peer bank earnings (cost-to-income, NIM trends)
Santos/gas policy implementation and Asia LNG demand

BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX share price vs. commodity correlation
WES.AX, CPL.AX pricing actions and volume trends
ASX small-cap mining cap raise activity (Canaccord, other brokers)
US 10Y yield and Fed rate hike probability
Chinese Arctic shipping and trade route developments
